struct Box_ { a: bool, b: bool, c: bool, d: bool }

struct Worker;

fn f() {}

// cyc_pos has nine ifs: cyclomatic 1 + 9 = 10.
fn cyc_pos(x: &Box_) {
    if x.a { f() }
    if x.b { f() }
    if x.c { f() }
    if x.d { f() }
    if x.a { f() }
    if x.b { f() }
    if x.c { f() }
    if x.d { f() }
    if x.a { f() }
}

// cyc_neg has eight ifs: cyclomatic 9.
fn cyc_neg(x: &Box_) {
    if x.a { f() }
    if x.b { f() }
    if x.c { f() }
    if x.d { f() }
    if x.a { f() }
    if x.b { f() }
    if x.c { f() }
    if x.d { f() }
}

// nest_pos nests four ifs: depth 4, one bump, cyclomatic 5.
fn nest_pos(x: &Box_) {
    if x.a {
        if x.b {
            if x.c {
                if x.d {
                    f();
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

// nest_neg nests three ifs: depth 3, one bump, cyclomatic 4.
fn nest_neg(x: &Box_) {
    if x.a {
        if x.b {
            if x.c {
                f();
            }
        }
    }
}

// bumps_pos has two separate top-level blocks that reach depth 2.
fn bumps_pos(x: &Box_) {
    if x.a {
        if x.b {
            f();
        }
    }
    f();
    if x.c {
        if x.d {
            f();
        }
    }
}

// bumps_neg has one nested block and one flat if.
fn bumps_neg(x: &Box_) {
    if x.a {
        if x.b {
            f();
        }
    }
    if x.c {
        f();
    }
}

// bool_pos has three boolean operators in one condition.
fn bool_pos(x: &Box_) {
    if x.a && x.b && x.c || x.d {
        f();
    }
}

// bool_neg has two boolean operators in one condition.
fn bool_neg(x: &Box_) {
    if x.a && x.b || x.c {
        f();
    }
}

// args_pos has five parameters.
fn args_pos(a: &Box_, b: &Box_, c: &Box_, d: &Box_, e: &Box_) {}

// args_neg has four parameters.
fn args_neg(a: &Box_, b: &Box_, c: &Box_, d: &Box_) {}

// prim_pos has four parameters, three of them primitive (75%): &str, i32, bool.
fn prim_pos(a: &str, b: i32, c: bool, d: &Box_) {}

// prim_neg has four parameters, two of them primitive (50%).
fn prim_neg(a: String, b: u8, c: &Box_, d: &Box_) {}

// prim_few has three primitive parameters: too few for the smell.
fn prim_few(a: &str, b: i32, c: bool) {}

// constructs uses every Rust decision point once: if / else if, while let, for,
// match arms beyond the first (the guard adds none), a let chain. loop nests
// but is not a decision point, and ? is not counted.
fn constructs(v: Option<i32>, xs: Vec<i32>) -> Option<i32> {
    if let Some(a) = v && a > 0 {
        f();
    } else if v.is_none() {
        f();
    }
    while let Some(y) = xs.pop() {
        f();
    }
    for i in 0..3 {
        f();
    }
    match v {
        Some(n) if n > 1 && n < 9 => f(),
        Some(_) => f(),
        None => f(),
    }
    loop {
        break;
    }
    let z = v?;
    Some(z)
}

impl Worker {
    fn method(&self, x: &Box_) {
        if x.a {
            f();
        }
    }

    fn associated(x: &Box_) {}
}

trait Speaker {
    fn speak(&self, x: &Box_) {
        if x.a {
            f();
        }
    }
}

// closures: the anonymous closure counts toward the function; run is a named
// closure and a unit of its own; inner is a nested fn and a unit of its own.
fn closures(x: &Box_) {
    let run = |y: i32| {
        if x.a {
            f();
        }
    };
    let apply = |g: &dyn Fn()| {
        if x.b {
            g();
        }
    };
    fn inner(x: &Box_) {
        if x.c {
            f();
        }
    }
    xs.iter().for_each(|e| {
        if x.d {
            f();
        }
    });
}
